title: Lola Young Announces 2027 Everything Begins Tour
excerpt: Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027.
body:
Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run scheduled for spring 2027. The tour opens at The Pinnacle in Nashville on April 6 and closes at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles on May 4, marking her first full headline run across the United States and Canada since she stepped away from touring in 2025.

The itinerary includes Radio City Music Hall in New York, two nights at Massey Hall in Toronto and the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium in San Francisco. Those rooms also show the jump in scale around Young's live career since "Messy" became her breakthrough hit. The tour name comes from her "Everything Ends" tattoo, reversing the phrase for a run built around her return to regular touring.

Young spent much of 2026 returning to the stage in shorter stretches. "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance at the Grammy Awards in February, and she later appeared at festivals including Rock in Rio, Reading and Austin City Limits. The new North American dates turn that gradual return into a dedicated headline schedule rather than another series of individual appearances.

New music has arrived alongside it. Young released "From Down Here" in May, her first new single since *I'm Only F**king Myself*. Produced by James Blake, the song was written the day after her Grammy win and found her looking at the uncertainty around success from a more hopeful position than much of the album that preceded it.

[youtube:YFhpMpONGUY]

Sofia and the Antoinettes will support the announced dates. Artist presales begin October 7, followed by the general sale on October 9 at 10 a.m. local time through Young's official site.

For Young, the route restores the kind of sustained North American schedule that disappeared when she cancelled her remaining shows in 2025. This time the return reaches some of the largest U.S. rooms she has headlined, with Radio City Music Hall and the Greek Theatre anchoring a run that now has new music alongside the songs that first expanded her audience.
